tagline: Sell a small catalog of products or digital files through your own storefront and Stripe Checkout.
verdictSummary: A product catalog, Stripe-hosted checkout, and gated file delivery after payment is a real, working store — and it's realistically a one-sitting build, since Stripe Checkout does the hardest part (card handling, PCI compliance) for you. What's missing is everything BigCommerce operates behind the scenes: tax calculation and remittance across jurisdictions, marketplace channels, and fraud tooling tuned across millions of transactions.
coreLoopDIY: Define products with prices and files or lesson content, send buyers to Stripe-hosted Checkout, verify the payment webhook, and grant time-limited download or lesson access on success.
whatYouLose: automatic sales tax calculation and remittance across states and countries
listing products on Amazon, eBay, and other marketplace channels from one dashboard
fraud detection tuned across BigCommerce's full transaction volume
built-in abandoned-cart recovery and marketing automation
24/7 support when a payment or delivery issue needs a human
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay for BigCommerce because tax is the actual hard part of selling online — correctly calculating and remitting sales tax across every jurisdiction a buyer might be in is a compliance problem, not a coding problem, and getting it wrong has real legal consequences. The subscription buys that compliance layer plus fraud and marketplace tooling, not just a shopping cart.
prompt:
Build a personal storefront: a product catalog, Stripe-hosted Checkout, and gated delivery of digital files or lesson access after payment. Stack: Next.js, PostgreSQL, Stripe Checkout and webhooks, S3-compatible storage for files.

Core loop: the operator defines products with a name, price, and either an attached file or lesson content, plus optional coupon codes. A buyer clicks purchase, is sent to Stripe's hosted Checkout page (so card data never touches your server), and on a verified `checkout.session.completed` webhook — checked against Stripe's signature and an idempotency key so a retried webhook can't double-grant access — the buyer's email is added as a customer with a signed, time-limited download or lesson-access URL. A refund or chargeback webhook revokes access. Keep an append-only order log for support and dispute handling.

Requires a Stripe account (test mode is free to build against) and S3-compatible storage for files. Sales tax is explicitly the operator's own responsibility — Stripe Tax can be enabled for a per-transaction fee, or the operator handles it manually; this build does not calculate or remit tax itself.

Do not build: multi-channel marketplace listings, fraud scoring beyond what Stripe already provides, abandoned-cart email sequences, or course/community features like discussion forums and certificates — those are separate products, not this one's scope.

faq.q: Can I import my existing BigCommerce catalog?
faq.a: BigCommerce exports products to CSV, and importing that into a matching schema is straightforward — the harder part is re-uploading digital files to your own storage, since BigCommerce doesn't hand those over in the export.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: As a responsive storefront, yes — Stripe Checkout itself is mobile-optimized. Managing the product catalog and orders from a phone is workable but not built for it.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Stripe takes its standard processing fee (around 2.9% + 30¢ per transaction) either way. Beyond that, hosting and storage run a few dollars a month — no separate platform fee like BigCommerce's monthly plan.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Tax compliance. BigCommerce calculates and can remit sales tax across jurisdictions automatically; here, that's either a paid Stripe Tax add-on or the operator's own legal responsibility to get right, and getting it wrong isn't a bug, it's a liability.
